text:
elaine: Opening a small docs PR to tighten Dedicated provisioning examples and add a Rust SDK + CLI example. Main goals: 1) show new field `max_concurrent_batches`, 2) add `isolation_level` enum docs, 3) fix a couple of anchors, and 4) add a migration note for field renames. Draft PR will be linked in a bit.

omar: Nice. I can take the CLI snippet and the console tooltip copy. Please call out that strict isolation disables burst by default and recommend pinning fallback models for regulated workloads.

jeff: I'll add the Rust SDK sample and a short note on event handling for preemption. We should standardize on the term "preemption" (not eviction) across the Dedicated docs.

anita: I'll review SLA wording and ensure the table clarifies that burst_capacity is best-effort and not covered by baseline SLA. Also will fix the crosslink from /dedicated/overview -> provisioning anchor.

docs-bot: link-checker: dedicated/provisioning.md -> broken anchor at line 195: `#capacityIsolation` (camelCase). Suggested anchor: `#capacity-isolation`.

elaine: thanks bot. I'll patch anchors and also add frontmatter `migration: yes` because we're renaming `max_batches` -> `max_concurrent_batches` and `burst_limit` -> `burst_capacity`.

omar: CLI example I'll add:
```bash
# create a scale policy via redwoodctl
redwoodctl dedicated scale-policy create \
  --name=fast-batch \
  --max-concurrent-batches=8 \
  --isolation-level=balanced \
  --burst-capacity=100
```
Include a short note: use `--isolation-level strict` to avoid burst (burst disabled).

jeff: Rust snippet draft:
```rust
let policy = ScalePolicy::builder()
  .name("fast-batch")
  .max_concurrent_batches(8)
  .target_latency_ms(100)
  .isolation_level(IsolationLevel::Balanced)
  .build();
client.dedicated().create_scale_policy(&policy).await?;
// subscribe to preemption events via client.events().on("preemption", ..)
```
I'll add a short mapping for old fields in migration section.

anita: SLA table edit suggestion: "Dedicated baseline capacity is covered by the committed SLA. Opportunistic burst_capacity is best-effort and not covered by the baseline SLA; under strict isolation preemption may route to pinned fallback models. Customers requiring strict uptime guarantees should provision baseline capacity accordingly." Will paste inline.

docs-bot: preview build: provisioning.md -> warnings: missing language tags for Rust and bash blocks; migration lint requires `migration: yes` in frontmatter.

ci-bot: CI preview: branch build passed after adding language tags. One remaining lint: avoid passive voice in the SLA paragraph.

elaine: updated PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/499. Tagged @jeff and @anita for review. Plan: merge after quick wordsmith and link fixes.

omar: I'll also add a short console tooltip draft for burst_capacity: "Burst capacity = short-lived excess throughput, best-effort, may be preempted under strict isolation"

jeff: after merge I'll follow up with a tiny PR adding the Rust snippet to the SDK examples index.

aneld: thanks team. Aim to merge today so Console can reference the updated docs for the UI tweak tomorrow.
